why_previous_wrong: Separated the prohibition, control, evidence, and fixture gate from the historical audit paragraph.
why_final_correct: Given one approved fixture for each media class, when ingestion runs, then each asset is indexed with its companions intact or returns a typed visible unsupported-format error, and every original hash is unchanged.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-01 and File 3 media gates.
correction_applied: Normalized overloaded audit text into a media-ingestion control.

previous_value: Writing stubs or mock production data to pass compilation.
final_value: Completed production paths must contain no stub success, todo macro, empty success return, or hard-coded mock dataset that substitutes for required behavior.
why_previous_wrong: Converted a governance audit paragraph into an observable completion prohibition.
why_final_correct: Given the changed production symbols, when the placeholder scan and focused behavior tests run, then no stub marker or dummy success remains and each required path produces real state-derived output.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-02 and LAM-INV-COMP-02.
correction_applied: Added a concrete scan and behavior gate.

previous_value: Completing Svelte screens with hard-coded mock data and no live IPC.
final_value: A completed target screen must obtain mutable or persisted state through its reviewed typed Tauri command and render the returned local data; hard-coded production mock state is prohibited.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the failure to the typed frontend bridge instead of a generic shell paragraph.
why_final_correct: Given seeded local state, when a user opens and exercises the target screen, then the expected reviewed command is invoked and the visible result reflects returned local data rather than a bundled mock.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-03 and Gate 5.
correction_applied: Created a live-data integration prohibition and criterion.

previous_value: Silently dropping XMP sidecar generation.
final_value: For every writable managed asset whose approved metadata is XMP-compatible, Lamha must write the co-located asset record and XMP mirror or expose a typed degraded state until reconciliation succeeds; silent XMP omission is prohibited.
why_previous_wrong: Separated XMP authority and degraded behavior from history.
why_final_correct: Given a writable managed asset with XMP-compatible metadata, when the sidecar transaction commits, then both sidecars exist with the expected revision or a visible degraded state identifies the failed mirror and retry path.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-04 and LAM-INV-ASSET-03.
correction_applied: Added transactional convergence and failure visibility.

previous_value: Creating physical category directories for people, groups, albums, or tags.
final_value: Event materialization must create only approved physical placement classes; people, group, album, and tag organization must remain virtual and must not create or duplicate category folders.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the prohibition to event filesystem materialization.
why_final_correct: Given assets assigned to people, groups, albums, and tags, when organization plans are simulated and committed, then no category directory or duplicate media copy is created and virtual memberships remain queryable.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-05 and event-folder rules.
correction_applied: Defined approved physical classes and a zero-copy gate.

previous_value: Automatically merging face clusters without user review.
final_value: Face-cluster analysis may create typed merge candidates, but Lamha must not persist a cluster merge until a user or an explicitly reviewed narrow rule approves it through the Review Centre.
why_previous_wrong: Moved the control from generic AI wording to face-cluster curation.
why_final_correct: Given two candidate face clusters, when the model proposes a merge, then identities remain separate until approval and only the approved Rust command persists the merge with provenance.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-06 and LAM-INV-AI-01.
correction_applied: Added proposal-versus-authority behavior.

previous_value: Exposing the local AI worker through a network listener.
final_value: The AI worker must communicate only through the reviewed private local transport owned by Rust and must not open an HTTP, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, or other listener reachable by unrelated clients.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the prohibition to the private worker transport package.
why_final_correct: Given the packaged worker on each supported platform, when Rust starts and exercises it, then requests complete through the private transport and socket inspection finds no listening network endpoint.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-07 and LAM-AI-001.
correction_applied: Specified transport, ownership, and observable listener absence.

previous_value: Overwriting the original filename during rename or move.
final_value: At ingestion Lamha must persist the original filename once in the authoritative asset record, and every later rename, move, relink, or restore must preserve that value unchanged.
why_previous_wrong: Reduced the audit paragraph to a write-once identity requirement.
why_final_correct: Given an ingested asset, when it is renamed, moved, relinked, and restored, then the current path changes as expected while originalFilename and its initial provenance remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-08 and LAM-INV-ASSET-05.
correction_applied: Added lifecycle triggers and an immutable observable.

previous_value: Deleting server infrastructure before callers and retained behavior are replaced.
final_value: Lamha must not remove a legacy subsystem until every retained caller has migrated, replacement behavior and applicable gates pass, and a dependency rescan proves the subsystem is no longer load-bearing.
why_previous_wrong: Created an explicit removal package and order gate.
why_final_correct: Given a legacy subsystem proposed for removal, when its removal package runs, then every retained caller points to a verified replacement and the final dependency/runtime scan reports zero load-bearing references before deletion begins.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-09 and replacement-before-removal guardrail.
correction_applied: Separated historical risk from the removal precondition.

previous_value: Treating rebuildable SQLite data as the only durable authority.
final_value: Lamha must persist approved user knowledge in its declared authoritative records and must be able to rebuild every derived SQLite index without losing those decisions.
why_previous_wrong: Separated durable authority from the destructive test setup.
why_final_correct: Given authoritative records containing approved decisions and a removed derived database, when rebuild runs, then the reconstructed indexes expose the same decisions and no authoritative value is missing or changed.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-10 and LAM-INV-META-03.
correction_applied: Added rebuild source and decision-equivalence verification.

previous_value: Moving or renaming linked-folder assets during organization.
final_value: Automated event organization and duplicate workflows must index linked-folder assets in place and must never move or rename them, regardless of filesystem writability.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the rule to the filesystem materialization boundary.
why_final_correct: Given a writable linked folder, when event and duplicate plans are simulated and committed, then every linked asset path and content hash remains unchanged while logical assignments are updated.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-11 and LAM-INV-EVENT-03.
correction_applied: Added trigger and path/hash preservation proof.

previous_value: Conflating camera owner with photographer.
final_value: Lamha must store camera owner and photographer as distinct attribution fields and must never copy, inherit, or overwrite one from the other without an explicit reviewed user action.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the rule to the attribution schema and importer.
why_final_correct: Given an asset whose camera owner and photographer differ, when metadata is imported and edited, then both identities and provenances remain distinct and changing either field leaves the other unchanged.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-12 and LAM-REMOVE-002.
correction_applied: Added distinct fields and independence criterion.

previous_value: Auto-populating visible people from event attendees.
final_value: Event attendee membership and asset-visible-person membership must remain separate authoritative relationships; neither may automatically populate the other.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the boundary to authoritative event records.
why_final_correct: Given an attendee who is not visible in an asset, when the event is linked to that asset, then the attendee remains on the event record and is absent from the asset visiblePersonIds unless separately approved.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-13 and LAM-REMOVE-003.
correction_applied: Defined separate authorities and a negative fixture.

previous_value: Dropping historical group membership dates.
final_value: Ending a group membership must close its active temporal interval at the approved effective date while preserving all prior intervals for historical queries.
why_previous_wrong: Separated temporal behavior from schema-history prose.
why_final_correct: Given a person with an active group interval, when the user ends membership on a chosen date, then that interval closes on the date and historical queries before the date still return the membership.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-14 and LAM-INV-PERSON-03.
correction_applied: Added end trigger and historical query observable.

previous_value: Flattening nested groups into a single-level list.
final_value: Lamha must preserve stable parent-group relationships and must reject any update that would create a group cycle; derived traversal may not flatten or replace the authoritative hierarchy.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned hierarchy authority to the group identity model.
why_final_correct: Given a three-level group hierarchy, when it is saved and rebuilt, then all parent links remain intact; when a cycle-forming update is attempted, Lamha rejects it without changing the last valid hierarchy.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-15 and LAM-GROUP-001.
correction_applied: Added rebuild preservation and rejected-update behavior.

previous_value: Claiming writes reached a read-only drive or throwing unhandled write errors.
final_value: When a root is read-only, Lamha must record the proposed change as a versioned pending overlay in application data, report its pending state, and reconcile only after root identity, revision, and conflict checks pass.
why_previous_wrong: Converted failure history into a detached-overlay state machine.
why_final_correct: Given a read-only root, when the user approves an edit, then the asset bytes remain unchanged, a pending overlay is visible, and later reconciliation applies only to the matching root and revision or returns a typed conflict.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-16 and LAM-EDGE-05.
correction_applied: Added pending-state and guarded-reconciliation observables.

previous_value: Automatically splitting a continuous event at midnight.
final_value: Midnight and time-gap heuristics may create an event-split proposal, but Lamha must preserve the existing event until a user approves a split; approved event start date controls folder naming.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the control to date and location boundaries.
why_final_correct: Given an event spanning midnight, when inference runs, then its membership and folder remain unified and any split appears only as a reviewable proposal until approval.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-17 and LAM-EDGE-06.
correction_applied: Added proposal state and no-mutation proof.

previous_value: Re-suggesting an equivalent rejected candidate after score drift.
final_value: Lamha must suppress an equivalent rejected candidate across routine reruns and score drift, and may reconsider it only after an explicit reopen or a material source, model, configuration, identity, or evidence change while preserving prior decisions.
why_previous_wrong: Separated suppression identity, allowed reopening, and history.
why_final_correct: Given a rejected candidate, when an equivalent task reruns with score drift, then no new review item appears; when a material reviewed input changes, a new linked candidate may appear and prior history remains queryable.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-18 and LAM-INV-AI-02.
correction_applied: Added equivalence and material-change criteria.

previous_value: Marking requirements complete after syntax checks alone.
final_value: A requirement may be marked complete only when every applicable gate has recorded command or inspection evidence, observable outputs, changed symbols, and reasoned not-applicable decisions.
why_previous_wrong: Converted the audit prose into a status transition invariant.
why_final_correct: Given a requirement proposed as complete, when the tracker validator runs, then each applicable gate links exact evidence and every omitted gate has an accepted not-applicable rationale; otherwise completion is rejected.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-19 and Gate 8.
correction_applied: Added exact evidence fields and rejection behavior.

previous_value: Leaving partial moves or corrupt sidecars after interruption.
final_value: Before a multi-file mutation, Lamha must durably prepare a transaction manifest, stage and verify outputs, commit atomically where possible, and recover or roll back by transaction identity after crash or disconnection.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the control to the crash recovery engine.
why_final_correct: Given a batch move with injected failure at each transaction stage, when Lamha restarts, then it reaches one consistent committed or rolled-back state with no missing original, partial sidecar, or untracked staged file.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-20 and LAM-TRANSACTION-001.
correction_applied: Added transaction sequence and consistent terminal states.

previous_value: Hardcoding platform-specific absolute paths.
final_value: Filesystem code must use OS-native path APIs and authorized root identities; it must not embed user-specific Windows, macOS, or Linux absolute paths.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the prohibition to cross-platform path adapters.
why_final_correct: Given Windows, macOS, and Linux simulated roots, when each path operation runs, then it resolves inside the authorized root with native semantics and rejects escape or malformed paths without a write.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-21 and Gate 4.
correction_applied: Added authorized-root and rejection behavior.

previous_value: Inventing cloud backup, remote sync, or multi-user login.
final_value: The final Lamha desktop runtime must operate locally without required cloud, remote synchronization, multi-user accounts, or server listeners; any separately approved outbound client must remain explicit, optional, and disabled by default.
why_previous_wrong: Mapped the scope prohibition to final outbound verification.
why_final_correct: Given a clean machine with networking blocked, when Lamha launches and exercises retained features, then no account or remote service is required and listener/outbound scans show only explicitly approved disabled-by-default clients.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-22 and scope-drift prohibition.
correction_applied: Added offline behavior and network observables.

previous_value: Asking the user to implement required code or TODOs.
final_value: An implementation package must either complete its authorized work and evidence or record a genuine blocker; it must not transfer required coding or verification work to the user as homework.
why_previous_wrong: Reclassified model-workflow history as a planning execution invariant.
why_final_correct: Given an authorized package, when execution ends, then the handoff contains completed evidence or a specific blocker with exhausted safe checks and contains no request for the user to write required implementation code.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-23 and LAM-INV-COMP-01.
correction_applied: Added terminal states and a transcript check.

previous_value: Guessing paths or inventing simplified schemas under ambiguity.
final_value: When required evidence is ambiguous, the implementation agent must preserve the known facts, record the exact unknown and affected record as blocked, and continue only independent work; guessed paths, fields, and schemas are prohibited.
why_previous_wrong: Converted informal workflow prose into a no-write invariant.
why_final_correct: Given an ambiguous path or schema obligation, when validation cannot resolve it from authoritative sources, then the affected item becomes BLOCKED with evidence and no guessed file, field, or write is produced.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-24 and anti-guessing guardrail.
correction_applied: Added blocked-state and no-guessed-output behavior.

previous_value: Reintroducing one category per person or guessing projections from labels.
final_value: Lamha must preserve multiple simultaneous and historical relationship edges with independent certainty, and must derive composition views only through explicit approved projection rules rather than relationship-label guesses.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned projection behavior to the relationship view package.
why_final_correct: Given a person with multiple historical edges, when composition views rebuild, then every edge and certainty remains queryable and only approved projection rules determine view membership.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-25 and LAM-REL-001.
correction_applied: Separated fact storage from derived view rules.

previous_value: Mutating primary media during non-destructive edits.
final_value: Crop, rotation, and color edits must update a versioned edit recipe and compatible metadata mirrors without modifying the primary media bytes; export must create a distinct derivative and must never silently overwrite the original.
why_previous_wrong: Separated edit authority from historical audit commentary.
why_final_correct: Given an asset and edit operations, when previews and exports are produced, then the original hash remains unchanged, reset restores the unedited view, and each export has a distinct derivative identity or a typed collision result.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-26 and LAM-INV-ASSET-01.
correction_applied: Added recipe, reset, hash, and derivative observables.

previous_value: Creating extra Master Plans or writing planning files into application code.
final_value: Lamha planning and generated semantic evidence must remain inside Graphify, application directories must contain no planning artifacts, and the authoritative Master Plan set must not be expanded by implementation tooling.
why_previous_wrong: Mapped the historical failure to active-plan write authority.
why_final_correct: Given the resolved Graphify and application roots, when planning tools run, then every created or modified planning path is inside Graphify and the application-tree inventory contains no new planning file.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-27 and directory-separation invariant.
correction_applied: Added resolved-root and inventory proof.

previous_value: Silently resolving conflicting metadata sources.
final_value: When authoritative records, embedded metadata, XMP mirrors, or pending overlays disagree, Lamha must preserve every source value and provenance, keep the last valid authority unchanged, and create a typed review conflict instead of silently choosing a winner.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned conflict handling to the authority-aware editor.
why_final_correct: Given conflicting JSON, XMP, embedded, and overlay values, when metadata is inspected or edited, then all values and sources are visible, the authoritative value remains unchanged, and resolution requires an explicit reviewed decision.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-28 and directional source-of-truth matrix.
correction_applied: Added preservation, visible conflict, and explicit resolution.

previous_value: Using one aiChecked boolean for all AI work.
final_value: Lamha must persist AI state per task with task type, state, model identity and version, model hash, source revision, configuration fingerprint, timestamps, and invalidation reason; a single aggregate aiChecked flag must not control validity.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned state authority to AI task persistence.
why_final_correct: Given two AI tasks using different model versions, when one model or source revision changes, then only affected task records become invalidated and the unaffected task remains current.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-29 and LAM-INV-AI-04.
correction_applied: Enumerated required fields and targeted invalidation.

previous_value: Materializing Mind Map drafts without confirmation.
final_value: Unsaved and saved Mind Map drafts must not mutate media folders; physical materialization requires an explicit simulation, validation, user confirmation, and durable filesystem transaction.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned physical execution to the simulation/materialization package.
why_final_correct: Given an unsaved or saved map draft, when nodes are edited and saved, then media paths remain unchanged; only a confirmed valid simulation may create a journaled materialization plan.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-30 and Mind Map state machine.
correction_applied: Added state transitions and no-mutation proof.

previous_value: Permanently deleting files when moved to Trash.
final_value: Moving a bundle to Trash must preserve the complete bundle in the reviewed root-scoped or cross-drive trash transaction; permanent deletion requires a separate explicit authorized action and must never occur during the trash move.
why_previous_wrong: Assigned the rule to trash and permanent-delete operations.
why_final_correct: Given a managed bundle, when the user moves it to Trash, then every bundle member is recoverable and no permanent delete runs; when an authorized permanent-delete action runs later, its plan and confirmation are separately recorded.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-31 and LAM-TRASH-001.
correction_applied: Separated operations and added recoverability proof.

previous_value: Stopping phase execution without a genuine blocker or stop instruction.
final_value: After a package and phase satisfy every applicable gate and record their evidence, execution may advance only to the next dependency-ready package; it must stop on a genuine blocker, explicit user stop, or missing authorization.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced ambiguous autonomy prose with bounded package transition rules.
why_final_correct: Given a completed package, when transition is evaluated, then the next action is the single dependency-ready authorized package or a recorded blocker/stop; no package is skipped or batch-started automatically.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 FAIL-32 and autonomous workflow rule.
correction_applied: Added safe transition outcomes and prohibited batch execution.

previous_value: OCR
final_value: When Lamha indexes OCR text, it must store the recognized text with asset identity, source region, model version, source revision, and confidence so local search can return traceable results and identify stale or unavailable OCR data.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a noun-only source clause into OCR indexing and staleness behavior.
why_final_correct: Given an asset with known text and a changed source revision, when OCR indexing and search run, then the matching asset and provenance are returned for the current revision and the stale entry is rejected or requeued.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 section 2.1 and CAN-LAM-AI-014 code evidence
correction_applied: Added actor, trigger, persisted fields, stale behavior, and fixture.

previous_value: Tags
final_value: When a local workflow proposes or changes a tag, Lamha must persist a namespaced, revisioned candidate or approved assignment, expose the decision state for review, and preserve the prior assignment if validation or storage fails.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a noun-only source clause into a revisioned review workflow.
why_final_correct: Given an asset with an existing tag, when a new tag candidate is approved and a storage failure is injected, then the prior assignment remains authoritative and the failed revision is visible for retry.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 section 2.1 and tag authority rules
correction_applied: Added review state, revision, and preservation behavior.

previous_value: Albums
final_value: When a user changes album membership or favorite state, Lamha must persist the affected asset relationship with a new revision, update the local view, and preserve the prior relationship if the authoritative write fails.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a noun-only source clause into album/favorite persistence behavior.
why_final_correct: Given an asset in an album, when membership is removed with an injected write failure, then the UI reports failure and the prior authoritative membership remains visible after reload.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 section 2.1 and album authority rules
correction_applied: Added user trigger, revision, UI result, and failure preservation.

previous_value: Renamed
final_value: When Lamha renames a managed asset, it must update the authorized current path through a journaled filesystem plan while preserving the original filename, stable asset identity, companion links, and original bytes.
why_previous_wrong: The prior viewer template treated a completed filesystem action as a UI label.
why_final_correct: Given a managed companion bundle, when an approved rename commits, then every planned path is updated, originalFilename and asset IDs remain unchanged, and rollback restores all paths after an injected failure.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 Asset Bundle Standard and operation-plan contracts
correction_applied: Reclassified rename as a journaled filesystem operation.

previous_value: Moved
final_value: When Lamha moves a managed asset, it must execute a validated journaled plan that preserves stable identity, original filename, companion links, metadata sidecars, and source bytes until destination verification succeeds.
why_previous_wrong: The prior viewer template omitted transaction and bundle-integrity behavior.
why_final_correct: Given a managed bundle and authorized destination, when a move fails before verification, then every source member remains intact and recovery reaches a complete source or verified destination state without a partial bundle.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 Asset Bundle Standard and file-operation plan contract
correction_applied: Reclassified move as a validated transaction with recovery.

previous_value: Reject
final_value: When a reviewer rejects a proposal, Lamha must persist the rejected transition, provenance, candidate fingerprint, and suppression scope while leaving authoritative metadata unchanged.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a button label into a persisted Review Centre transition.
why_final_correct: Given a pending proposal, when the user rejects it, then reload shows the rejected decision and an equivalent routine rerun does not create a new pending item.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 section 15.3 and Review Centre state rules
correction_applied: Added decision persistence, authority preservation, and suppression.

previous_value: GPS
final_value: When privacy removal targets GPS metadata, Lamha must create a reviewed mutation/export plan that preserves source provenance and the managed original while removing approved coordinate fields only from the selected output or authoritative revision.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a noun-only privacy field into a scoped removal workflow.
why_final_correct: Given an asset with embedded, JSON, and XMP coordinates, when a privacy-clean export is approved, then the export contains none of the selected GPS fields, the managed original hash is unchanged, and the recipe records every removed field.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 section 30.2 and privacy-removal contracts
correction_applied: Added scope, preservation, output, and recipe evidence.

previous_value: Scan
final_value: Before the initial scanner package exits, Lamha must scan a fixture root containing supported, unsupported, nested, hidden, unreadable, and symlinked entries and report indexed, skipped-with-reason, and rejected counts without changing any source byte.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word gate with an adversarial scanner acceptance test.
why_final_correct: Given the reviewed scanner fixture, when the scan runs, then every entry has one typed outcome, symlink escape is rejected, counts reconcile to the fixture inventory, and all source hashes remain unchanged.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 24.3 and initial scanner package
correction_applied: Added fixture composition, typed outcomes, counts, and integrity proof.

previous_value: Maintain
final_value: When any requirement or package status changes, the completion tracker must preserve prior revisions and record the actor, timestamp, evidence links, applicable gates, and resulting status transition.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word tracker gate with revisioned status behavior.
why_final_correct: Given an existing tracker row, when its status changes, then the new revision links its predecessor and evidence while the previous revision remains queryable.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 28 and active-plan authority package
correction_applied: Added trigger, required fields, and history verification.

previous_value: Use
final_value: Destructive actions must use the shared typed confirmation contract with explicit target summary, consequence text, authorization token, collision behavior, and cancel path; feature-specific duplicate dialogs must be removed after parity proof.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word removal gate with the retained confirmation behavior and deletion condition.
why_final_correct: Given each destructive action, when confirmation is opened, cancelled, and approved, then the shared contract displays the exact targets, cancellation writes nothing, and approval invokes only the typed authorized command.
evidence: Master Plan File 2 section 37 and trash/permanent-delete contracts
correction_applied: Defined shared behavior, observable cancel/approve paths, and removal prerequisite.

previous_value: Tests
final_value: Every actionable canonical requirement must identify at least one focused verification that exercises its success or preservation behavior and names the owning work package.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word extraction field with a traceability requirement.
why_final_correct: Given the active canonical registry, when traceability validation runs, then every actionable row links a focused verification and an existing owning package or an explicit reviewed exception.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 10 and active registry contract
correction_applied: Added scope, required links, and validator result.

previous_value: Proof
final_value: Every actionable canonical requirement must link exact observable evidence or a reasoned not-applicable decision for each required gate before its status can become complete.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word proof field with a completion invariant.
why_final_correct: Given a requirement proposed as complete, when proof validation runs, then exact evidence exists for every applicable gate and any missing or generic proof blocks completion.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 10 and tracker proof rules
correction_applied: Added evidence granularity and blocking behavior.

previous_value: Keep
final_value: For every discovered production capability, the bottom-up audit must record the exact current paths and symbols, the retained behavior, its target owner, and verification evidence before classifying it as kept.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word audit category with the evidence needed for a keep decision.
why_final_correct: Given the discovered production inventory, when bottom-up audit validation runs, then every kept capability has path/symbol evidence, a target owner, and a verification link.
correction_applied: Added classification inputs and completeness validation.

previous_value: Remove
final_value: For every discovered legacy capability proposed for removal, the bottom-up audit must record exact paths, retained callers, replacement owner, removal condition, and absence verification before authorizing deletion.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word audit category with replacement-before-removal evidence.
why_final_correct: Given the discovered production inventory, when removal-audit validation runs, then every removal row has a verified replacement and zero unresolved retained callers; otherwise deletion remains blocked.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 20.2 and removal guardrail
correction_applied: Added callers, replacement, removal condition, and blocking result.

previous_value: XMP
final_value: When Lamha reads or writes an XMP mirror, it must preserve the authoritative value and provenance, validate the mirror revision, and surface missing, malformed, stale, or conflicting XMP as a typed degraded or review state without discarding the last valid authority.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a noun-only source clause into an authority-aware XMP read protocol.
why_final_correct: Given valid JSON authority and malformed or conflicting XMP, when metadata inspection runs, then JSON remains unchanged, the XMP problem is visible with provenance, and a repair or review action is available.
evidence: Master Plan File 1 original metadata rules and sidecar read protocol
correction_applied: Added read/write trigger, validation, degraded state, and preservation.

previous_value: Test
final_value: Each high or critical risk must link a runnable failure or boundary test that demonstrates its mitigation and identifies the package gate that the test can block.
why_previous_wrong: Replaced a one-word risk field with a risk-to-test traceability gate.
why_final_correct: Given the active risk register, when risk validation runs, then every high or critical risk links an existing runnable check and owning package gate; a missing link fails validation.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 section 26 and risk register
correction_applied: Added risk severity scope, runnable check, owner, and failure behavior.

previous_value: Do not edit, move, create, or delete anything in Codebase/.
final_value: During the read-only provenance and planning boundary, every application path outside Graphify must remain byte-for-byte unchanged and every generated evidence path must resolve inside Graphify.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a short historical boundary gate into the current resolved-root integrity contract.
why_final_correct: Given the initial outside-Graphify SHA-256 inventory, when planning validation finishes, then a fresh inventory reports zero added, removed, modified, or renamed application paths and the write-guard escape fixtures fail.
correction_applied: Added resolved scope, byte integrity, and guard rejection evidence.

previous_value: Do not mark complete before double-check and proof.
final_value: A work package must not transition to complete until its focused checks, affected regression checks, required boundary and recovery checks, and exact evidence links have been independently validated against its exit gate.
why_previous_wrong: Expanded a short completion warning into an observable package transition rule.
why_final_correct: Given a package proposed as complete, when completion validation runs, then every applicable check and evidence link passes and any missing, stale, or generic proof leaves the package incomplete.
evidence: Master Plan File 3 risk management and completion gates
correction_applied: Added required check classes and blocked transition behavior.

previous_value: Implementation must honor this constraint: Local AI Worker (LAM-AI-001): A bundled local child process executing machine-learning inference. The desktop application launches and supervises it; it exposes no HTTP, WebSocket, TCP, or UDP listener, uploads no media or private metadata, requires no cloud service, and remains unavailable to unrelated external clients. Phase 1 selects the non-network local IPC mechanism after mapping the existing transport, lifecycle, streaming, cancellation, cross-platform, packaging, and security constraints. Permitted candidates include standard input/output, named pipes, Unix-domain sockets, Tauri sidecar communication, or another validated non-network mechanism.
final_value: Informational trace only; no active implementation phase or package.
why_previous_wrong: Generated wrapper asserted behavior or proof without a record-specific actor, trigger, observable result, and failure criterion.
